overall_summary: The homepage overwhelms first‑time visitors with dense navigation, generic messaging, weak trust cues, and unclear calls to action, which likely hampers conversion.

findings.title: Overloaded navigation and copy
evidence: navigation list includes dozens of links: Products, Solutions, Developers, Company, Pricing, Contact, Chat Messaging, Video & Audio, Activity Feeds, AI Moderation, Vision Agents, plus many solution sub‑pages (Dating, Education, Financial, Gaming, etc.)
hero sections repeat long copy such as "Build Chat, Video, Feeds and Moderation. Install the Stream skill to ship in minutes and scale to billions."
findings.interpretation: The sheer number of options and repeated text creates cognitive overload, making it hard for users to identify the primary product and next step.
findings.hypothesis: Decision paralysis reduces the likelihood that a visitor will click a conversion CTA, lowering sign‑up rates.
findings.recommendation: Streamline the top navigation to a few core items and consolidate solution links under a single dropdown; reduce duplicate hero copy.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the current nav with: Products, Solutions, Pricing, Contact, Get Started. Collapse solution categories into a hover menu.

findings.title: Unclear primary call‑to‑action above the fold
evidence: hero text includes "Get started Talk to an expert" but no distinct button label is captured in the data.
CTA section later reads "Start building in-app experiences for free. Get started Talk to an expert" without visual hierarchy.
findings.interpretation: Visitors cannot quickly discern the recommended action, leading to hesitation or exit.
findings.hypothesis: Ambiguous CTA reduces click‑through to the signup flow, decreasing conversion rates.
findings.recommendation: Add a prominent, contrasting primary CTA button that states the exact next step, e.g., "Start Free Trial".
findings.suggested_change: Replace the generic "Get started" text with a large button labeled "Start Free Trial" placed directly under the hero headline.

findings.title: Generic product messaging without clear benefits
evidence: Repeated phrases like "Build any in-app chat or messaging. SDKs for fully customizable UI" and "AI skill for faster development" appear without concrete outcomes.
No copy directly addresses pain points such as time‑to‑market, cost savings, or reliability beyond technical specs.
findings.interpretation: The copy tells what the product does but not why it matters to the buyer, limiting perceived value.
findings.hypothesis: Potential customers may not see a compelling reason to choose Stream over competitors, leading to lower intent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite hero and sub‑headings to focus on benefits, e.g., "Launch chat in days, not weeks, with 99.999% uptime".
findings.suggested_change: Change hero sub‑text to: "Ship fully‑featured chat, video, and feeds in minutes, backed by 99.999% uptime and zero hidden limits."

findings.title: Insufficient trust signals beyond technical stats
evidence: Social proof section only lists metrics: "1B+ end users 99.999% uptime SLA 8ms median API response".
No customer logos, testimonials, or case‑study excerpts are present in the captured data.
findings.interpretation: Technical performance data alone may not reassure new buyers; they often look for recognizable brand endorsements.
findings.hypothesis: Lack of social proof can increase perceived risk, causing prospects to abandon the site.
findings.recommendation: Add a carousel of well‑known client logos (e.g., eBay) and short quote testimonials on the homepage.
findings.suggested_change: Insert a section titled "Trusted by" with logos of eBay, Coinbase, etc., followed by a quote: "Stream reduced our chat development time by 80%."
